cards.title: Structured Population Models for Heterogeneous Resistance
cards.claim: Physiologically Structured Population (PSP) models can describe resistance as a selection process based on heterogeneous binding affinities (e.g., K_D distributions) among cells. In this framework, resistance is defined by a critical affinity (K_Dcrit); bacteria with K_D > K_Dcrit survive and grow, while those with K_D < K_Dcrit are killed. This approach models adaptive resistance as a selection of pre-existing heterogeneity rather than a single-step mutation.
conditions: Applicable only when binding-affinity heterogeneity is a supported mechanistic hypothesis; selection of this model requires biological justification.
Requires assumptions about receptor turnover and binding equilibrium.
Static drug concentration assumption simplifies the model but may be violated if bacterial load clears drug.
required_inputs: Distribution of binding affinities (K_D) within the bacterial population.
Maximum efficacy and critical concentration parameters.
Time-kill data for strains with differing susceptibilities.
limitations: This is a specific mechanistic hypothesis (binding affinity selection); it does not apply to all resistance mechanisms (e.g., efflux pumps, enzymatic degradation).
Numeric parameters (e.g., K_Dcrit values) are specific to the studied strain/drug pair and cannot be reused.
Model assumes exponential growth of the resistant subpopulation.
cards.downstream_use: Use PSP models when investigating adaptive resistance driven by molecular heterogeneity. Do not apply this specific mathematical framework to drugs with different mechanisms of action without re-deriving the structural assumptions.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Time-kill, regrowth and resistance mechanism interpretation

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
